names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 1 iunie, «Sfântul Cuvios Agapit de la Lavra Pecerska».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 1 Ιουνίου, «Όσιος Αγαπητός ο εν τω σπηλαίω ο Ανάργυρος και Ιαματικός ο εκ Ρωσσίας», with the rank word and the three epithets left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 1. јун ст. ст., „Преподобни Агапит Печерски“ — Преподобни is the `venerable` this corpus puts in `types` and is stripped; Печерски is the house and not a rank, so it stays and the form is the fullest the heading gives. MEASURED, AND THE FULLER FORM AVOIDS A LIVE FOLD: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Агапит Печерски» but `[('agapitus-of-rome', 'sr'), ('agapitus-the-deacon', 'ru')]` for the bare «Агапит», so the bare form would have folded onto a pope of Rome on the strength of a forename.

Name page 53 heads him «Преподобный Агапит Печерский, врач безмездный», which is the only name page of this day to spell the rank out rather than abbreviate it; «Преподобный» is the rank and «врач безмездный» the grade, so both come off and the two name words remain. 'agapit pecherski' is the Serbian form already on this folder and folds apart from this one; 'агапит печерскии' has no other holder.

death.note: doxologia.ro's life closes: «Pomenirea Sfântului Agapit se săvârșește la 1 iunie (ziua fericitei sale adormiri, veacul al XI-lea) și la 28 septembrie (Soborul Sfinților din Peșterile de Aproape).» No closer year is printed. The Охридски пролог for 1. јун ст. ст. does print one, and it is the only one of the three books that does: „Упокоји се свети Агапит око 1095. године“. The interval is left at the century, because 1095 falls inside it — so there is nothing to widen and adopting it would narrow another book's own range — and because „око“ is an approximation and not a source for an endpoint (5 October 2026).

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 1 июня ст. ст. — «Прп. Агапита Печерского, врача безмездного (XI).»

attestations.note: The day's fourth entry of seven, «Прп. Агапита Печерского, врача безмездного (XI).». «врача безмездного» — the unmercenary physician — is the `unmercenary` and `physician` this folder already carries in `types`, and the century «(XI)» is the 11th century the folder already holds. The identification is the menologion day, the Печерский epithet and the physician's grade together, and the folder's own Romanian life already closes on the 1 June commemoration. The day page prints a troparion and a kontakion under his name, both specifying «в Ближних пещерах», in the Nearer Caves, and both are added. `id53`, the index of his lives, was NOT followed, so nothing of his life is touched here. azbyka.ru was not read.

feast.note: doxologia's life page says he is kept twice: «la 1 iunie (ziua fericitei sale adormiri, veacul al XI-lea) și la 28 septembrie (Soborul Sfinților din Peșterile de Aproape)». The folder keeps 1 June, the day the calendar page prints him on; the 28 September synaxis of the Near Caves is recorded here and is not rendered as a second feast (24 September 2026).

saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Ιουνίου — «Όσιος Αγαπητός ο εν τω σπηλαίω ο Ανάργυρος και Ιαματικός ο εκ Ρωσσίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 1 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the corpus already keeps him on, and it is plainly the same man: «έζησε στη Ρωσία περί τον 11ο αιώνα μ.Χ. και ασκήτεψε στη Μεγάλη Λαύρα του Κιέβου στα χρόνια του Οσίου Αντωνίου», which is the folder's own century and monastery, and the unmercenary physician the folder's `types` already carry. **The Greek adds the one patient it names**: «θεράπευσε και τον πρίγκιπα του Τσέρνιγκωφ Βλαδίμηρο Βσεβολόντοβιτς, ο οποίος αργότερα έγινε μεγάλος πρίγκιπας του Κιέβου με την επωνυμία «Μονομάχος»», and the resting place of the relics in the cave of Saint Anthony. `dates` are not replaced: the folder's eleventh century is the same reading this page gives, and the page adds no year. The Anthony it cross-refers to on 10 July is the folder's existing `related` row. No hymn is printed for him.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 14.06.2026 (1. јун ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Агапит Печерски“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. THE SHORTEST OF THE THREE ACCOUNTS AND IT DIFFERS FROM THE FULLEST IN TWO PLACES. „Безмездни врач. Ученик светог Антонија Печерског“ corroborates `unmercenary`, `physician`, `monk` and the one `related` row this folder has. New: it makes the Armenian THE PRINCE’S OWN PHYSICIAN („кнежев лекар, неки Јерменин“) where doxologia makes him a famous physician of Kyiv; it says plainly that Agapitus healed the prince („Тако излечио и кнеза Владимира Мономаха“) where doxologia has him beg not to be sent to Chernigov and the roots carried there by the messengers; and it says the herbs he gave were the ones he made his own bread from. `кнез` IS NOT A ROW: Vladimir Vsevolodovich Monomakh is the object of a healing and no calendar read for this corpus keeps him — `vladimir-the-great` is another man, dead in 1015 — and a prince healed is not a kinship and not a martyrdom. He is already in this folder’s prose off both earlier books, unlinked, and gains nothing. The Armenian is unnamed in all three books and gets neither row nor folder. „око 1095“ RECORDED IN THE NOTE AND NOT WRITTEN INTO THE INTERVAL, AND THIS IS THE ONE THING ON THIS DAY THE AUTHOR MIGHT WANT DIFFERENTLY. „Упокоји се свети Агапит око 1095. године“ is THE ONLY YEAR ANY OF THE THREE BOOKS HAS PRINTED for him; doxologia gives «veacul al XI-lea» and saint.gr «περί τον 11ο αιώνα». The interval is LEFT at 1001 to 1100 and the display at «11th century», for two stated reasons: 1095 is inside the century the other two give, so there is nothing to widen and taking it would NARROW another book’s range; and „око“ is an approximation, which this wave has four times refused as a source for an endpoint. The Prologue’s sentence is added to the `death` note instead, so the year is in the record and the reader can see which book printed it. `types` untouched, all four corroborated or unaffected. No `office`, no `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Богоноснаго Антония ревнуя смиренномудрию,/ аки некиим врачевством зелием снедным/ исцелял еси болящия, преподобне Агапите,/ тем и врача неверна уверив,/ наставил еси на путь спасения./ Уврачуй и наша болезни/ и молися Господеви о воспевающих тя.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, «Тропарь преподобного Агапита Печерского, врача безмездного, в Ближних пещерах», глас 5, under «Молитвы» on the day page for 1 июня ст. ст. It names him in the vocative, so it is his own proper. It also names «Богоноснаго Антония», to whom this folder is already related.

english.text: Emulating the humble wisdom of the God-bearing Anthony, thou didst heal the sick as with some medicine, by herbs given for food, O venerable Agapitus; and bringing thereby an unbelieving physician to faith, thou didst set him on the way of salvation. Heal our sicknesses also, and pray to the Lord for those who sing thy praise.

hymns.text: Врач сый изряден, чудне,/ являя несумненную твою веру,/ обличая же армениново неверие/ и приводя его к благочестию,/ себе, близ смерти бывшу,/ испросил еси от Бога продолжение живота/ и, сим чудом того уверив,/ привел еси Христови,/ Емуже в веселии предстоя,/ молися о нас, преподобне.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, «Кондак преподобного Агапита Печерского, врача безмездного, в Ближних пещерах», глас 6, under «Молитвы» on the day page for 1 июня ст. ст. The «арменин» it reproves is the unbelieving Armenian physician of his life, whom this folder's own life already tells of.

english.text: Being an excellent physician, O wondrous one, thou didst show forth thy unwavering faith, reprove the Armenian's unbelief and lead him to piety; and being thyself near to death thou didst ask of God a lengthening of thy life, and having by that wonder brought him to believe, thou didst lead him to Christ, before whom thou standest in gladness: pray for us, O venerable one.
